stem: Which artery is the most common source of the sinoatrial (SA) nodal artery?
explanation: The SA nodal artery arises from the right coronary artery in roughly 60% of people and from the left circumflex artery in most of the remainder, so the right coronary artery is the most common source.

optionAnalysis.A: Correct. The right coronary artery gives rise to the SA nodal artery in about 60% of people.
optionAnalysis.B: Incorrect. The left anterior descending artery supplies the anterior left ventricle and anterior septum; it is not the usual source of the SA nodal artery.
optionAnalysis.C: Incorrect. The posterior interventricular artery supplies the inferior parts of the ventricles and the posterior septum.
optionAnalysis.D: Incorrect. The left marginal artery is a branch of the left circumflex artery supplying the lateral left ventricle.
optionAnalysis.E: Incorrect. A diagonal branch comes off the left anterior descending artery and supplies the anterolateral left ventricle.

clinicalPearl: Proximal right coronary artery disease can disturb sinus node function, one reason inferior infarcts are often accompanied by bradycardia.
learningObjectives: Name the usual arterial supply of the sinoatrial node.

stem: In a right-dominant coronary circulation, from which vessel does the posterior interventricular (posterior descending) artery arise?
explanation: Coronary dominance is defined by the artery that gives rise to the posterior interventricular artery. In right dominance, which is the most common pattern, this is the right coronary artery.

optionAnalysis.A: Correct. In right dominance the right coronary artery gives off the posterior interventricular artery.
optionAnalysis.B: Incorrect. The left anterior descending artery runs in the anterior interventricular groove.
optionAnalysis.C: Incorrect. The left circumflex artery gives rise to the posterior interventricular artery only in left dominance.
optionAnalysis.D: Incorrect. The left main artery divides into the left anterior descending and left circumflex arteries.
optionAnalysis.E: Incorrect. The acute marginal artery is a branch of the right coronary artery supplying the right ventricle.

clinicalPearl: Dominance determines which territory is affected by an occlusion near the crux of the heart, so it matters when interpreting infarct patterns.

stem: Occlusion of the left anterior descending artery most directly compromises the blood supply to which region?

options.text: Anterior wall of the left ventricle and the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum
Posterior wall of the left ventricle
Free wall of the right atrium
Inferior wall of the right ventricle

explanation: The left anterior descending artery runs in the anterior interventricular groove and supplies the anterior wall of the left ventricle and the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum.

optionAnalysis.A: Correct. This is the territory of the left anterior descending artery.
optionAnalysis.B: Incorrect. The posterior left ventricle is supplied mainly by the left circumflex or posterior interventricular artery.
optionAnalysis.C: Incorrect. The sinoatrial node is supplied by the SA nodal artery, usually from the right coronary artery.
optionAnalysis.D: Incorrect. The right atrial free wall is supplied by right coronary artery branches.
optionAnalysis.E: Incorrect. The inferior right ventricle is supplied by right coronary artery branches.

clinicalPearl: Because it supplies so much left ventricular muscle, proximal left anterior descending occlusion carries a large infarct burden.
learningObjectives: Describe the territory supplied by the left anterior descending artery.

stem: Which valve lies between the left atrium and the left ventricle?
explanation: The mitral (bicuspid) valve guards the left atrioventricular orifice, between the left atrium and the left ventricle.

optionAnalysis.A: Incorrect. The tricuspid valve lies between the right atrium and right ventricle.
optionAnalysis.B: Correct. The mitral valve is the left atrioventricular valve.
optionAnalysis.C: Incorrect. The aortic valve lies between the left ventricle and the aorta.
optionAnalysis.D: Incorrect. The pulmonary valve lies between the right ventricle and the pulmonary trunk.
optionAnalysis.E: Incorrect. The coronary sinus valve guards the opening of the coronary sinus into the right atrium.

clinicalPearl: The mitral valve is the only atrioventricular valve with two cusps.
learningObjectives: Locate each of the four heart valves.
